the single seam that owns the tier state machine, so a client never juggles raw

against the resource's manage authority; an unsupported state for the type (e.g.
Open on a secret) is a 422, a lack of authority a 403.

post.description:
Bind a project and register its webhook.

Refusals are a CLOSED set. The previous ``except Exception`` reflected
``str(e)`` verbatim, which handed an authz denial's reasoning and a
credentials-store fault's internals to the caller.

The registration handshake and every later delivery, one door.

The handshake is the only unsigned request Asana ever makes here — there is
no secret yet to sign with — so it is admitted ONLY against a window an
admin's bind opened moments ago, identified by a ticket that exists nowhere
but in the target URL we handed Asana. An unsolicited handshake, a handshake
after the window closed, and a second handshake against a burnt window are
all refused with the same uniform answer.

once the target is authorized; below the tier that creating the same
connector would take it is 403, and a malformed target is 400.

Re-probe every saved connector and persist refreshed health. Health only
— recheck never re-snapshots capabilities.

asking is neither possible nor already in flight the field is omitted entirely

RequestedPermission.title: RequestedPermission
RequestedPermission.description:
The abstract access a member asks for — NOT a literal relation/permission
string. ``USE`` maps (per type, via the schema seam) to the USE-conferring
relation; ``GOVERN`` maps to the type's governance tier (MANAGE for content/
secret/mcp, EDIT for the runtime skill/agent family); ``WRITE`` maps to the
optional tier between them, which only a type declaring one offers (today
``code_repo``, where it is what authorizes a run to commit). The access BC stays
free of per-type relation names by routing all three through ``resolve_grant``.

S3Config.title: S3Config
S3Config.description:
The S3 object-store platform connector's scope: ONE bucket, a REQUIRED
prefix allowlist, and the bucket's region. Endpoint URLs are constructed
from these fields alone, so their syntax is validated strictly — a hostile
bucket or region string is the only SSRF surface this connector has.

The allowlist is required because its absence used to mean "the whole
bucket": the widest possible reach was the value you got by leaving a field
out. Scope is now something you state.

S3StorageBackend.title: S3StorageBackend
S3StorageBackend.description:

The IAM user keys live in the Credentials BC (provider ``AWS`` /
auth-scheme ``ACCESS_KEY_SECRET``); only the reference is held here.

SearchHitResponse.description:

SharePointConfig.title: SharePointConfig
SharePointConfig.description:
The SharePoint platform connector's scope: a REQUIRED site allowlist
plus the Graph search region.

``region`` is not decoration — Microsoft Graph makes it MANDATORY on
``/search/query`` whenever the request carries application permissions
(§12 checkpoint), so an app-only search without it is a 400 on every call.

``site_ids`` is the reach boundary WE enforce. App-only search is granted
tenant-wide (``Sites.Read.All``); ``Sites.Selected`` is not supported by
``/search/query``. Graph therefore cannot scope the query for us — the
server restricts by site and drops every hit outside this list.
